data.hypothesis: Explicitly selecting CUB's BLOCK_REDUCE_WARP_REDUCTIONS policy may perform better than the previously measured default CUB BlockReduce policy by changing how each 128-thread CTA combines its four warps. This tests a distinct CTA-local policy while keeping launch geometry, one-value-per-lane loading, stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy fixed; only complete-run measurements can establish whether it helps.

memory_lessons.applicability: This experiment holds the CTA and multi-stage topology constant while varying the CUB reduction policy.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior default-CUB candidate measured 29.215 μs and the explicit warp-centric candidate measured 30.066 μs, each over three samples and with all correctness cases passing. Those results favor the default-CUB candidate in those runs, but do not establish the cause or predict the result of another policy.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this policy with the same complete-run protocol and compare its repeated timings and correctness against both prior candidates.

data.notes: The controller reports the prior default-CUB mean as 29.215 μs, the explicit warp-centric mean as 30.066 μs, and the baseline as 46.787 μs; all were valid and correct. This candidate is not yet measured, so no speedup is claimed. Comparing complete-run timings isolates the local algorithm policy from launch topology, although unchanged stages and launch/copy costs may still affect the total.
transformations: Add the CUB BlockReduce header and instantiate BlockReduce<T, 128, cub::BLOCK_REDUCE_WARP_REDUCTIONS> for the CTA-local sum.
Provide exactly one input value per lane, using zero for out-of-range tail lanes to preserve tail safety.
Retain the 128-thread launch, dynamic shared-memory launch argument, multi-stage scratch schedule, scratch selection, and final copy unchanged.
